spec.name: Warhound 77 Armored Hauler
spec.description: A low-poly cyberpunk militarized 6x6 truck from 2077 with armored cab, roof turret, neon trim and a modular cargo bed.
spec.layout: A long, heavy 6x6 hauler facing +Z. Front: a wedge armored hood with a glowing cyan light bar, a slatted grille, a plow bumper and a winch. Behind the hood is a tall angular cab with slit windshield glass and side armor skirts, and a roof turret with twin barrels pointing forward. Behind the cab is a long cargo bed with container ribs, hazard stripes, a missile pod rack and rear light cluster. Three axles of big chunky wheels (front, mid, rear) with a wheel arch over each, resting on y=0. Style: faceted angular plates, matte dark gunmetal hull with yellow hazard trim, magenta and cyan neon strips, small glowing vents, antennas, panel seams and rivets painted by place (soot near exhaust, wear on edges, mud at wheels). Everything is built from boxes, wedges, extrudes and lathes with chunky blocky shapes and many small fittings.

parts.builds: Ladder frame and underbody from y=0.35 to 1.25: two long rails, cross members, axle housings and differentials at the three axles, drive shafts, fuel tanks and battery boxes on the sides, exhaust stacks with soot paint, side armor skirts with panel paint and hazard-stripe edges, mud-paint on lower faces. Also the floor deck plate at deckTop with seam paint.
parts.attaches: Deck at deckTop carries cab, bed; wheel arches align to axle mounts.

parts.builds: Six big chunky wheels (radius 0.55, width 0.5), each on its wheel joint: faceted 10-sided tyre lathe with tread blocks, steel rim with bolt ring, hub cap with a glowing cyan ring, brake disc and caliper visible, mud paint at the bottom. Front pair slightly wider hubs with steering knuckle blocks. Spare fittings: wheel fender flaps behind each wheel. Rear and mid wheels may be a dual-wheel pair on each side.
parts.attaches: Each wheel centred on its axle mount at y=0.55 and its wheel joint.

parts.builds: Hood and nose from z=2.0 to 4.0: wedge sloped armored hood, grille with vertical slats and cyan glow behind, plow bumper with hazard-stripe teeth, winch drum and cable hook, twin headlight slits (glowing white) plus magenta underglow strip, fender wheel arches over front wheels, hood vents with ember glow, small antennas, tow hooks, number plate decal, armor rivet paint.
parts.attaches: Starts at chassisFront and meets the cab at z=2.0, resting on the deck.

parts.builds: Tall angular armored cab from z=-0.6 to 2.0, y=1.25 to 2.9: faceted sloped roof, slit windshield with SVG glass reflection texture and wiper, side windows with armored shutters, doors with panel seams and handles, mirrors with cameras, roof rack with searchlights and antennas, side step, interior hint (seats, dash with glowing screens via glow), hazard-stripe trim, a roof hatch ring at turretRing, unit emblem decal on doors.
parts.attaches: Sits on the deck at cabFloor; front edge meets frontEnd; rear edge meets cargoBed at cabBack; roof ring supports the turret at turretRing.

parts.builds: Roof-mounted remote weapon station on turretYaw and gunPitch: ring base with gear teeth, armored faceted housing, sensor eye with glowing red lens, twin autocannon barrels with muzzle brakes, ammo box with belt feed, ejection port, side missile launcher tubes, hazard stripes, a small antenna and radar dish, painted wear on edges. Barrels point +Z to the muzzle mount.
parts.attaches: Ring base sits on cab roof at turretRing (z=0.9).

parts.builds: Armored modular cargo bed from z=-4.0 to -0.7, y=1.25 to 2.6: container shell with vertical ribs, hinged side panels, roof hatches, hazard stripes, orange cargo straps, stacked crates and a strapped fuel drum on top, missile pod rack with six tubes angled up, side tool lockers with latches, corporate emblem decals and stencil text SVG textures, cyan neon edge strip, antenna array, panel seam paint with rust and soot.
parts.attaches: Front wall touches the cab at cabBack; floor sits on deckTop; rear ends at bedRear.

parts.builds: Rear of the truck from z=-4.0 to -3.4 plus the rear bumper: tail light cluster (red glow) with magenta strip, heavy rear bumper with step and hitch ball, tow chains, rear ramp door with hinges and big hazard chevron decal, license plate decal, exhaust stacks up the rear corners of the bed with ember glow, mud flaps, rear camera and a spare tyre on a rack, rear sensor light bar.
parts.attaches: Meets cargoBed at bedRear; bumper hangs from chassis end.

calls.reasoning:
I'm working out the wheel placement for a six-wheeled build, positioning joints along the ±X axis at specific offsets and sizing each wheel's radius and width to fit within the body's box dimensions.

Now I'm designing the wheel geometry itself using a lathe profile rotated around the axle axis, defining the tyre's radius and width as a closed polygon, then adding a smaller rim disc and a glowing hub cap accent inside it.

For bolts I'm considering generating them as a ring of small cylinders around each hub, but with six wheels and eight bolts each (48 parts) plus tread blocks, I'm wary of blowing the part budget, so I'm counting up the per-wheel component cost to stay under the limit.

I'm working out how to merge bolt and tread geometries into single meshes using matrix transforms so each wheel only costs a couple parts instead of dozens, computing joint positions from known axle coordinates and building the tread blocks as a ring of boxes positioned around the wheel's rotation axis.

Still modeling wheel geometry...

I'll add mud paint to the tyre using a mix of rubber and rust colors blended with noise and a vertical smoothstep gradient, then start on fender flap boxes.

Placing rear and front fender flaps behind the wheels, checking clearance offsets so they don't clip into the body, then adding front knuckle blocks and a wider front hubcap. I'm also checking how the lathe-based wheel geometry's bottom vertices align with the floor at ten segments.

I'm adjusting tread block positions so their radius stays just inside the tire's outer radius without poking through the floor plane, then moving on to writing the joint reference code and merged part definitions.

Attaching parts to their bones with flat color assignments—steel, rim, neon cyan, rubber for treads, red for calipers, steel for discs. I'm checking the lathe axis orientation so the tire profile revolves symmetrically with the correct outward direction.

I'm planning out the turret part structure, figuring out joint placements for the yaw and pitch mechanisms relative to the body and cab roof, using static bone references for the ring base.

Now I'm sketching the box dimensions for the turret body, barrel extensions, and muzzle positions, then outlining the construction helpers for building each geometric piece with lathe shapes and merged box geometry for gear teeth.

Writing turret housing geometry...

For the hull paint, I'm combining mottle texture with countershading for depth. Then I'm adding hazard stripes diagonally across a trim band, and planning a glowing red sensor lens pod mounted on the housing's side using a rotated cylinder.

Now I'm building out the gun assembly: paired barrel rods with thicker shrouds, a muzzle brake with slits, cooling rings as small cylinders, and a mantlet block to anchor it all to the pitch mechanism.

I'm also placing the ammo box to the side on the turret bone, then planning a belt feed from the ammo box to the gun using small link boxes along a curved sweep, keeping the belt attached to the pitch bone while the ammo box stays on the turret yaw.

Now I'm detailing side features: a dark ejection port near the housing, and on the opposite side a missile launcher block with four forward-facing tube cylinders in dark olive, balanced against the ammo box on the other flank.

I'm also placing a short antenna rod near the top of the housing with a white tip, staying within the height budget, plus a small tilted radar dish built from a lathe bowl profile at the rear.

For the ring base I'm adding a thin cyan glow strip, likely using a slim torus shape rotated flat to sit at the housing's front edge.

Then I'm shaping the gun housing's profile, placing the barrel center around y3.2 with a sloped front and rear mantlet, and adding a thin hazard stripe box near the rear slope for detail.

Positioning rivet spheres along the housing's top edge in a merged group for the side detailing, then building the gear teeth as small rotated boxes placed around the gear radius using matrix transforms.

For the muzzle brake, I'll use a box with two darker thin boxes on the sides to suggest slits. I also need to import glow from the kit's glow path.

I'm planning to keep the front-end build reliable by sticking with basic geometry primitives like box and extrude, and loosely typing the context parameters to avoid friction.

Now I'm sketching out the hood shape as an extruded wedge profile, defining the slanted outline coordinates to create the sloped front and sides. I'm also planning the paint treatment with seams, rivets, and weathering, then laying out the body parts—hood plate with a raised ridge, and fenders arched over the front wheels using a cylinder segment approach.

I realize the cylinder-based arch leaves a one-sided visibility problem, so I'm switching to an extruded arc profile instead, building the outer and inner radius points to form the fender shell shape and checking that its position doesn't clash with the hood's width.

Adjusting the fender and wheel arch dimensions to fit within the body bounds, then adding a fender top plate to connect the arch to the hood, and sketching out a glowing grille recess with vertical slats for the front of the hood.

Still shaping the plow bumper and hazard-light teeth geometry...

I also need to work out the winch drum placement relative to the bumper face, adjusting the bumper's z-depth so the drum sits flush without poking through the front boundary.

Adjusting the hood, bumper, and grille profiles so they stack correctly in y and z -- raising the bumper top slope and shifting the grille panel upward so they don't overlap.

Now I'm adding the winch drum and hook details near the front bumper, sizing them so they stay within the bumper's z bounds, plus a thin cable-wrap cylinder. I'm also planning the magenta underglow as thin strips along the underside and front, and figuring out the hood vent geometry as recessed boxes following the hood's sloped surface.

Mapping out slats...

Now I'm placing the small details: red tow hooks as tiny torus shapes on the front bumper, a number plate decal plane offset to one side to avoid the winch, and thin antenna rods mounted on the fenders.

I'm figuring out antenna height limits against the body box constraints, aiming for a whip antenna with a glowing red tip ball, then thinking about hood side armor plates with rivet details—using painted texture for most rivets and a few merged bolt geometries along the fender edges via mergeGeometries from three/addons.

Now I'm placing the headlight housings as dark boxes with yellow trim bars, then working out fog light and winch positions on the bumper to avoid overlap—settling on the winch drum centered at x=0, a side plate at x=-0.62, and fog lights spaced outward around x=±0.85 to -0.95.

Finalizing bumper layout: fog lights at x±0.98, tow hooks at ±1.2, and the plate simplified to just x=0.62. I'm then adding hazard teeth across the bumper bottom, cyan neon glow strips along the hood sides near the fender arches, and a magenta glow strip running under the front bumper.

A dark undertray box under the hood, a firewall box marking the cab-front interface, and confirming the hood extrudes correctly from its base. I'm also sketching out the helper function for building boxes with glow materials, keyed to joint coordinates for absolute positioning.

Realizing painted parts can't glow, so I switch to writing a paint function for the hull using mix/noise/smoothstep utilities, computing seams by dominant normal and adding mud discoloration near the bottom and lighter tones toward the top. Then I start on the hazard stripe pattern using diagonal coordinate math.

Still writing part geometry...

I'm positioning the fender geometry to overlap slightly with the hood, adding a flat top plate for the fender cap and figuring out how the hood's side walls and width should extend to cover the gap without visible seams.

Adjusting the front block profile so it tucks under the hood slope properly, then placing a light bar on the hood's front face and sketching a grille centered on the front block.

Headlights go at ±1.05 width, y1.2. For rivets, I'm merging small sphere geometries using BufferGeometryUtils along the fender and front block edges into a single grouped mesh. For the ember vents, I'm layering a glowing inner box with dark slat boxes across the front, generated through loops.

I need to fix pieces that exceed the box boundaries—the lockers stick out past x limits by up to 0.24, and the crate stacking goes too high, pushing past the y max. I'm recalculating the crate stack heights so the roof stays within bounds, and still need to address the drum, antennas, missile rack, and locker positioning.

Shrinking the drum from height 0.7 to 0.45 with a lower center so the top sits around 2.85 instead of overshooting to 3.13, and adjusting the rings and cap offsets to match. For the missile tubes, I'm reducing length and recentering them along with the rack plates and muzzle rings so the tilted geometry stays under the ceiling, then trimming the antenna heights down to 0.3-0.45 so their tips stop clearing the box at 3.3 and instead land closer to 2.85.

Now I'm pulling the lockers inward slightly so they don't poke past the panel edges, nudging the box, front face, latch, bolt, and glow positions a few centimeters to stay within tolerance, and tightening the hazard box and neon trim thickness to match.

I'm seeing a lot of pieces positioned way outside the expected bounds, which points to an offset miscalculation relative to floorY and the roof height. The real culprit seems to be the pillar extrusions being oriented along the wrong axis, so the thickness is running along x instead of the intended direction.

I need to lower roofY, shrink the antenna and searchlight heights, and recenter the pillars so nothing pokes above the max height of 3 or beyond the drawing bounds.

Adjusting windows, windshield frames, headlights, visor, and mirror y-positions down to fit under the new lower roof height while keeping seats and dashboard proportions intact.

Now I'm checking x-extents on mirrors, side steps, and skirt extrusions to make sure nothing pokes too far beyond the body width, tightening mirror offset to 1.48 and centering cab extrude thickness symmetrically rather than offset.

Roof plate extrusions and antenna/hatch positioning look fine, as does the wiper placement relative to floor height. Now I just need to write out the actual edits, making sure each search string matches the source exactly.
